questions.q: Which three qualities does Maxwell say trust is mainly built on?
a: Honesty, fairness and good judgement
Charisma, confidence and ambition
Experience, authority and results
Loyalty, courage and discipline
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the three, noting they are connected and that fairness is the easiest to start with.

questions.q: What happens when a leader decides the rules do not apply to them?
a: Trouble follows, as it did for Richard Nixon
They gain respect for acting decisively
Their followers trust them even more
They rise faster through the ranks
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses Nixon’s illegal break-in as the example of a leader placing himself above the law.

questions.q: How does the summary say a leader keeps earning respect over time?
a: By loyally putting followers’ well-being first
By staying ahead of everyone in skill
By rewarding the most loyal followers
By avoiding any show of weakness
questions.why: Lesson 2 says initial respect must be renewed by devotion to the people you lead.

questions.q: What earned Gandhi lasting respect, according to the summary?
a: He risked his own safety at every protest he led
He avoided violence in every speech he gave
He persuaded foreign leaders to support him
He refused to lead more than one campaign
questions.why: Lesson 2 highlights that he kept putting himself in harm’s way alongside his followers.

questions.q: What does Churchill’s career show about leadership, according to the summary?
a: Repeated losses need not stop a leader from winning
Early failure usually predicts later defeat
Winning elections matters more than winning wars
A leader should hide setbacks from followers
questions.why: Lesson 3 traces his many defeats and his eventual wartime partnership with the US.
